scope: Proposition 9.2 (Rounding and metric realization) of the manuscript “Squared-logarithmic randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics” (preprints/Squared-logarithmic-randomized-k-server-on-arbitrary-metrics-September-24-2026/Squared-logarithmic-randomized-k-server-on-arbitrary-metrics-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 110 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 db9f0de04f757cf3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 59-60. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the fractional allocations and anchors constructed in the preceding sections, with τ ≥ 22. They admit a causal rounding satisfying (9.1) for which Nrnd := E H ∑ t=1 ∑ v̸=root r|v|−1|nv(t) − nv(t − 1)| ≤ 132V. (9.7) 59 Placing the integer parks at their current anchors gives simulated configurations St of exactly k members containing each current request. There is a matching of consecutive configurations with expected total cost at most 120Nrnd + 40Tanchor. (9.8) Consequently their expected movement is at most C(V + ℓP + ℓQ) + D for an absolute C and a finite additive term D depending only on the fixed finite structure.
